title: Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce's Formula 1 Team Has Garage Broken Into - NewsBreak
text:
By Arman Khan ,
4 minutes ago
Alpine, the Formula 1 team backed by high-profile investors Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, and several other elite athletes, faced an unexpected security incident this week after two individuals broke into one of its facilities in Viry-Châtillon, Essonne.
According to Le Parisien , the two individuals entered the garage area of Alpine’s engine and technical base during the late-night break-in. Local authorities responded quickly, locating the two individuals inside the premises.
The Alpine F1 team works in the garage during practice ahead of the 2024 Bahrain Grand Prix. (Photo by Peter Fox - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)
Police are still investigating the motive behind the break-in, but initial indications suggest it was not an attempt to sabotage the team or steal sensitive F1 data.
The Extent of Damage The individuals smashed a window in the entrance vestibule and gained access to the building’s lobby. Once inside, the intruders did not remain on the ground floor; instead, they made their way directly to the upper level, where the offices of the Alpine F1 team’s executives and management are located.
The Evry prosecutor’s office confirmed that an investigation is underway, noting that no arrests have been made at this stage. The Territorial Crime Division (DCT) has been assigned to lead the inquiry.
Mechanics work on the car of Alpine's French driver Pierre Gasly in the garage before the second practice session at the 2025 Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix. (Photo by MOHD RASFAN/AFP via Getty Images)
Inside the facility, several office doors were reportedly forced open. The intruders appeared to have moved through multiple rooms, searching the premises as if they were familiar with the base's layout.
Despite the intrusion, those close to the team insist that the situation is under control. “Nothing was stolen. Everything is fine. There were no employees present at the time,” a source close to the F1 team told Le Parisien. Another source echoed the reassurance, stating, “There was no theft.”
Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce: Why They Invested in Alpine F1 The incident has drawn added media interest because Alpine’s ownership includes two of the NFL’s biggest stars. Mahomes and Kelce joined an investment group in 2023 as part of a €200 million funding round that brought several global sporting icons into Formula 1, including Boxing star Anthony Joshua and Golf icon Rory McIlroy .
Anthony Joshua celebrates after beating Otto Wallin during the Day of Reckoning: Fight Night at Kingdom Arena. (Photo by Richard Pelham/Getty Images)
At the time, Patrick Mahomes spoke about why he wanted to be part of the Alpine project, saying, "I’ve always had a passion for all sports. The opportunity to lead an investor group with Travis in Alpine F1 alongside Otro Capital was one I couldn’t pass up."
"It’s an exciting time for the sport, and this is an opportunity to bring our shared values to the world stage. I’m looking forward to being a part of its growth," the Chiefs' QB concluded.
Patrick Mahomes, Otro Capital Alpine F1 Team Investor and Kansas City Chiefs player, and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, walk in the paddock at the 2024 Miami Grand Prix. (Photo by Kym Illman/Getty Images)
Travis Kelce also expressed enthusiasm about entering the sport: “I am thrilled to lead an investor group and join forces with Patrick and the team at Otro Capital on this exciting venture with Alpine F1. Our shared passion for excellence and innovation forms the cornerstone of this partnership.”
"It’s about being able to contribute to a sport that demands precision, teamwork, and relentless pursuit of success. I am looking forward to this new chapter and can’t wait to see what we achieve together," the Chiefs' TE added.
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce (87) looks on against the Arizona Cardinals during the first half at State Farm Stadium.Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images
Their involvement helped strengthen Alpine’s global appeal, especially among American audiences.
With the break-in under investigation, Alpine and its drivers, Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto, now turn their attention back to tightening security and preparing for the remaining races of the 2025 season .
